name: Bruna Morse
life: “I still remember the morning a payroll transfer stopped halfway through.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Bruna by a small Saturday habit. Bruna knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I ran payroll. I warned management on Wednesday and told the crews on Friday. I can't get Thursday back.
appearance: Bruna is easy to recognize by auburn hair cut square at the nape and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a striped cotton shirt with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges, Bruna rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Bruna always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Bruna is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To tell the crew exactly when management got the warning.
family: Anton Dove is Bruna’s half-sibling. Bruna can always ask for five minutes alone. Anton asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Window seven*, Anton says, “Window seven is the first place I saw the sea after I moved here.”
connections: Penelope Jeong. The manager's daughter hears which day the payroll worker knew about the shortfall. Also in the story is Simon Hunter (freight worker).

reactions.situation: A worker asks to give their account privately
reactions.response: Bruna arranges a one-to-one account and checks which facts the worker permits to be shared.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Bruna says what they know in their own name and refuses to treat a guess as something the child has to disprove.

reactions.situation: If somebody tries to repay an old favor all at once
reactions.response: Bruna suggests a smaller gesture they can repeat without hardship.
